shared.concept_anchor: Natural pigments used in Ajanta paintings

en.display_text:
Consider the following statements about the pigments and materials used in Ajanta paintings:

1. Ochre, used as a yellow and red pigment at Ajanta, was sourced locally from the Deccan region and did not require long-distance trade.
2. Lapis lazuli, the source of vivid blue colour in Ajanta paintings, was imported from Afghanistan — specifically the Badakhshan region — since no comparable deposits exist in India.
3. Cinnabar, used as a red pigment at Ajanta, is derived from copper oxide and was available in abundance throughout the Deccan plateau.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 only
(b) 1 and 2 only
(c) 2 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: Ochre, used as a yellow and red pigment at Ajanta, was sourced locally from the Deccan region and did not require long-distance trade.
statement_analysis.reason: Ochre is an iron oxide mineral available in the Deccan region; it is documented as a locally sourced pigment at Ajanta, unlike lapis lazuli which had to be imported.

statement_analysis.statement: Lapis lazuli, the source of vivid blue colour in Ajanta paintings, was imported from Afghanistan — specifically the Badakhshan region — since no comparable deposits exist in India.
statement_analysis.reason: Badakhshan (in modern Afghanistan) was the ancient world's primary source of lapis lazuli and supplied India, Persia, Egypt, and Rome; Indian mines do not produce lapis lazuli.

statement_analysis.statement: Cinnabar, used as a red pigment at Ajanta, is derived from copper oxide and was available in abundance throughout the Deccan plateau.
statement_analysis.reason: Cinnabar is mercury sulfide (HgS), not copper oxide; the confusion with copper compounds is a common error. Cinnabar is not abundantly available in the Deccan and was a more precious, specifically sourced pigment.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option d (all three correct) is deceptive because statements 1 and 2 are both correct and students who have learned the general pigment list may not scrutinise Statement 3's chemical description carefully.
elimination_logic: Statement 1 is correct — ochre is a locally available iron oxide pigment in the Deccan.
Statement 2 is correct — lapis lazuli from Afghanistan (Badakhshan) is well-documented as an Ajanta import.
Statement 3 is incorrect — cinnabar is mercury sulfide, not copper oxide; this is a chemical misidentification.
Only Statements 1 and 2 are correct, matching option b.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 3's trap exploits the limited chemistry knowledge most humanities students bring to art-history questions. Copper compounds are also used as pigments (malachite, azurite) and are sometimes associated with Deccan mining. Stating cinnabar is a 'copper oxide' sounds plausible to someone who knows it is a mineral pigment but has not memorised the precise chemistry. The correct identification — mercury sulfide — is the discriminating fact.
en.final_explanation:
The palette of Ajanta painters was built from a combination of locally available and long-distance imported mineral pigments, each chosen for its specific colour quality and stability.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Ochre, produced from iron oxides (goethite for yellow, hematite for red), is native to the Deccan basalt region. Its local availability made it the most economical pigment in the Ajanta palette.
• Statement 2 — Correct: Lapis lazuli's extraordinary deep blue required importation from the Badakhshan mines of Afghanistan — one of the most important evidence points for Ajanta's international trade connections.
• Statement 3 — Incorrect: Cinnabar is mercury sulfide (HgS), not copper oxide. Copper-based pigments (such as malachite) are different compounds. Cinnabar's red was brilliant but relatively rare; its chemical identity as a mercury compound is a precise fact that UPSC questions sometimes test.

Value Addition:
• Lamp black (carbon soot) was used for outlines and dark tones; white lime provided highlights.
• The binding medium for pigments was derived from animal glue (hide or bone) or plant gums, not egg-based as in European tempera.
• The use of burnishing with an agate stone on the final painted surface created the characteristic lustrous finish of Ajanta murals.

hi.display_text:
अजंता चित्रों में उपयोग किए गए रंगों और सामग्रियों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:

1. ओकर, जो अजंता में पीले और लाल रंग के रूप में उपयोग किया जाता था, स्थानीय रूप से डेक्कन क्षेत्र से प्राप्त किया जाता था और इसके लिए लंबी दूरी का व्यापार आवश्यक नहीं था।
2. लैपिस लाजुली, जो अजंता चित्रों में जीवंत नीले रंग का स्रोत है, अफगानिस्तान से आयातित था — विशेष रूप से बादाख़शान क्षेत्र से — क्योंकि भारत में इसके समान खनिज नहीं पाए जाते।
3. सिनाबर, जो अजंता में लाल रंग के रूप में उपयोग किया जाता था, तांबे के ऑक्साइड से प्राप्त होता है और डेक्कन पठार में प्रचुर मात्रा में उपलब्ध था।

उपरोक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?

(a) केवल 1
(b) केवल 1 और 2
(c) केवल 2 और 3
(d) 1, 2 और 3

statement_analysis.statement: ओकर, जो अजंता में पीले और लाल रंग के रूप में उपयोग किया जाता था, स्थानीय रूप से डेक्कन क्षेत्र से प्राप्त किया जाता था और इसके लिए लंबी दूरी का व्यापार आवश्यक नहीं था।
statement_analysis.reason: ओकर एक लौह ऑक्साइड खनिज है जो डेक्कन क्षेत्र में उपलब्ध है; यह अजंता में स्थानीय रूप से प्राप्त रंग के रूप में प्रलेखित है, जबकि लैपिस लाजुली को आयात करना पड़ता था।

statement_analysis.statement: लैपिस लाजुली, जो अजंता चित्रों में जीवंत नीले रंग का स्रोत है, अफगानिस्तान से आयातित था — विशेष रूप से बादाख़शान क्षेत्र से — क्योंकि भारत में इसके समान खनिज नहीं पाए जाते।
statement_analysis.reason: बादाख़शान (आधुनिक अफगानिस्तान में) प्राचीन विश्व का मुख्य लैपिस लाजुली स्रोत था और भारत, फारस, मिस्र, और रोम को आपूर्ति करता था; भारत के खदानों में लैपिस लाजुली नहीं मिलता।

statement_analysis.statement: सिनाबर, जो अजंता में लाल रंग के रूप में उपयोग किया जाता था, तांबे के ऑक्साइड से प्राप्त होता है और डेक्कन पठार में प्रचुर मात्रा में उपलब्ध था।
statement_analysis.reason: सिनाबर पारा सल्फाइड (HgS) है, तांबे का ऑक्साइड नहीं; तांबे के यौगिकों के साथ भ्रम एक सामान्य त्रुटि है। सिनाबर डेक्कन में प्रचुर मात्रा में उपलब्ध नहीं था और यह एक अधिक मूल्यवान, विशेष रूप से प्राप्त रंग था।

hi.strong_distractor: d — विकल्प d (तीनों सही) भ्रमित करने वाला है क्योंकि कथन 1 और 2 दोनों सही हैं और जो छात्र सामान्य रंग सूची जानते हैं वे कथन 3 के रासायनिक विवरण को सावधानी से नहीं देख सकते।
elimination_logic: कथन 1 सही है — ओकर डेक्कन में स्थानीय रूप से उपलब्ध लौह ऑक्साइड रंग है।
कथन 2 सही है — अफगानिस्तान (बादाख़शान) से लैपिस लाजुली अजंता में आयात के रूप में अच्छी तरह प्रलेखित है।
कथन 3 गलत है — सिनाबर पारा सल्फाइड है, तांबे का ऑक्साइड नहीं; यह रासायनिक गलत पहचान है।
केवल कथन 1 और 2 सही हैं, जो विकल्प b से मेल खाते हैं।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: कथन 3 का जाल अधिकांश मानविकी छात्रों की सीमित रसायन विज्ञान ज्ञान का उपयोग करता है जो कला-इतिहास प्रश्नों में लाते हैं। तांबे के यौगिक भी रंगों के रूप में उपयोग होते हैं (मलाकाइट, अजुराइट) और कभी-कभी डेक्कन खनन से जुड़े होते हैं। सिनाबर को 'तांबे का ऑक्साइड' कहना उस व्यक्ति के लिए संभावित लगता है जो जानता है कि यह एक खनिज रंग है लेकिन सटीक रसायन विज्ञान याद नहीं रखता। सही पहचान — पारा सल्फाइड — निर्णायक तथ्य है।
hi.final_explanation:
अजंता चित्रकारों का रंगपेटी स्थानीय रूप से उपलब्ध और लंबी दूरी से आयातित खनिज रंगों के संयोजन से बनी थी, प्रत्येक को उसके विशिष्ट रंग गुण और स्थिरता के लिए चुना गया था।

• कथन 1 — सही: ओकर, जो लौह ऑक्साइड से बनता है (पीले के लिए गोएथाइट, लाल के लिए हीमेटाइट), डेक्कन बेसाल्ट क्षेत्र का स्वदेशी है। इसकी स्थानीय उपलब्धता ने इसे अजंता रंगपेटी में सबसे किफायती रंग बनाया।
• कथन 2 — सही: लैपिस लाजुली का असाधारण गहरा नीला रंग अफगानिस्तान के बादाख़शान खदानों से आयातित था — जो अजंता के अंतरराष्ट्रीय व्यापार संबंधों के लिए एक महत्वपूर्ण साक्ष्य बिंदु है।
• कथन 3 — गलत: सिनाबर पारा सल्फाइड (HgS) है, तांबे का ऑक्साइड नहीं। तांबे आधारित रंग (जैसे मलाकाइट) अलग यौगिक हैं। सिनाबर का लाल रंग चमकीला था लेकिन अपेक्षाकृत दुर्लभ था; इसका रासायनिक स्वरूप पारा यौगिक के रूप में एक सटीक तथ्य है जिसे UPSC प्रश्न कभी-कभी परखते हैं।

Value Addition:
• लैम्प ब्लैक (कार्बन कालिख) का उपयोग रूपरेखा और गहरे रंगों के लिए किया गया; सफेद चूना हाइलाइट के लिए।
• रंगों के लिए बाइंडिंग माध्यम पशु गोंद (चमड़ा या हड्डी) या पौधों के गोंद से प्राप्त होता था, यूरोपीय टेम्परा की तरह अंडे आधारित नहीं था।
• अंतिम चित्रित सतह पर अगेट पत्थर से रगड़ने का उपयोग अजंता भित्ति चित्रों की विशिष्ट चमकदार सतह बनाता था।

shared.concept_anchor: Aniconic to iconic transition — Karla as transitional site

en.display_text:
Consider the following statements about the iconographic evolution across rock-cut Buddhist cave sites:

1. The early Buddhist caves at Bhaja contain no anthropomorphic images of the Buddha because the aniconic convention — representing the Buddha through symbols such as the bodhi tree, stupa, and footprints — had not yet been replaced by figural depiction.
2. Karla represents a fully iconic phase of Buddhist art, with multiple anthropomorphic images of the seated Buddha displayed prominently within the chaitya hall.
3. The introduction of Bodhisattva figures such as Padmapani and Vajrapani into Buddhist art is associated with the Mahayana phase and represents a doctrinal shift from the earlier Hinayana emphasis on the monk's solitary path.

Which of the above statements is/are NOT correct?

(a) 1 only
(b) 1 and 3 only
(c) 2 and 3 only
(d) 2 only

statement_analysis.statement: The early Buddhist caves at Bhaja contain no anthropomorphic images of the Buddha because the aniconic convention — representing the Buddha through symbols such as the bodhi tree, stupa, and footprints — had not yet been replaced by figural depiction.
statement_analysis.reason: Bhaja belongs to the aniconic phase of early Hinayana Buddhist art (2nd century BCE); the absence of Buddha images is intentional and doctrinally motivated, not a technical limitation.

statement_analysis.statement: Karla represents a fully iconic phase of Buddhist art, with multiple anthropomorphic images of the seated Buddha displayed prominently within the chaitya hall.
statement_analysis.reason: Karla is characterised as a transitional site — it retains the aniconic stupa at the centre but shows some early figural elements on the facade. It is not a 'fully iconic' phase site; multiple seated Buddha images inside the hall are not a feature of Karla's chaitya.

statement_analysis.statement: The introduction of Bodhisattva figures such as Padmapani and Vajrapani into Buddhist art is associated with the Mahayana phase and represents a doctrinal shift from the earlier Hinayana emphasis on the monk's solitary path.
statement_analysis.reason: Bodhisattva figures are a Mahayana innovation, reflecting the doctrinal emphasis on helping all beings achieve liberation; they appear in the later phase caves at Ajanta and are absent from Hinayana-era sites.

en.strong_distractor: a — Option a (Statement 1 only) is deceptive because students who know Statement 2 is wrong may also start doubting Statement 3 as an oversimplification, leading them to select only Statement 1 as incorrect.
elimination_logic: Statement 1 is correct — Bhaja's aniconic character is a well-established fact about early Hinayana art.
Statement 2 is NOT correct — Karla is transitional, not 'fully iconic'; describing it as having 'multiple anthropomorphic images of seated Buddha inside' is a fabricated scope-extension.
Statement 3 is correct — Bodhisattva figures as a Mahayana innovation is a standard art-historical fact.
Only Statement 2 is NOT correct, making option d the answer.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2's scope-extension trap takes the real fact of Karla's transitional character and inflates it into a false claim of 'fully iconic' status with multiple Buddha images. Students who know Karla is 'more elaborate than Bhaja' and 'less elaborate than later Ajanta' may still be unsure where exactly the iconic threshold was crossed, and the confident language of Statement 2 may cause them to accept it as true.
en.final_explanation:
The aniconic-to-iconic transition in Buddhist art was gradual, spanning several centuries, with different sites occupying different positions on that continuum.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Bhaja's complete absence of anthropomorphic Buddha imagery is a defining feature of the earliest phase of rock-cut Buddhist art, reflecting the doctrinal convention of aniconism.
• Statement 2 — NOT Correct: Karla is a transitional site — its chaitya is centred on an aniconic stupa (as at Bhaja), but the facade shows some early figural elements. Karla does not have multiple anthropomorphic Buddha images inside the hall; describing it as 'fully iconic' misrepresents its position in the iconographic evolution.
• Statement 3 — Correct: The Bodhisattva concept is distinctly Mahayana and its artistic expression (Padmapani, Vajrapani, Maitreya) appears only in later caves at Ajanta, not in Hinayana-era sites.

Value Addition:
• The Kushana-period schools of Gandhara and Mathura are credited with establishing the anthropomorphic Buddha image as a canonical form in the 1st–2nd century CE.
• The transition from aniconic to iconic is not merely artistic — it reflects a profound theological shift in how the Buddha's transcendence was conceptualised.
• At Bhaja, relief carvings of Vedic-style figures (Surya, Indra) appear on an exterior veranda, showing the complex religious environment of early Buddhism.

en.display_text:
Assertion (a): A period of approximately 300 years separates the two distinct phases of excavation at Ajanta — the earlier Hinayana phase and the later Mahayana phase — during which no significant new excavation was undertaken at the site.

Reason (R): The Vakataka dynasty, particularly under the reign of Harishena, served as the principal royal patron of the Mahayana-phase excavations and artistic programme at Ajanta.

(a) Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A
(b) Both A and R are correct, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
(c) A is correct but R is incorrect
(d) A is incorrect but R is correct
elimination_logic: Step 1: Is A correct? Yes — a gap of approximately 300 years between the end of the Hinayana-phase excavations and the beginning of the Mahayana-phase excavations at Ajanta is an accepted historical fact.
Step 2: Is R correct? Yes — the Vakataka dynasty, particularly under Harishena, was the principal patron of the Mahayana-phase excavations; this is well-documented.

Step 3: Does R explain A? No — R explains who resumed Ajanta excavations in the 5th–6th century CE, but it does not explain WHY there was a 300-year gap. The gap is attributed to the decline of Satavahana power, the rise and preoccupation of intervening dynasties, and the shift in royal patronage patterns — not to the Vakatakas' eventual arrival. R is a fact about the resumption, not a cause of the interruption.
A correct + R correct + R does NOT explain A → option b.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: This is a causation-direction trap. R correctly identifies who resumed Ajanta's excavations, and students who read both A (gap exists) and R (Vakatakas resumed it) naturally assume R explains A, because the Vakataka intervention 'broke' the gap. But R identifies the agent of resumption, not the cause of the gap itself. The cause of the gap lies in the collapse of Satavahana patronage and the absence of a successor patron with the interest and resources to continue — a different historical explanation entirely.
en.final_explanation:
Ajanta's peculiar two-phase structure — with a 300-year silence between them — is one of the most discussed puzzles in Indian art history.

• Assertion (a): Correct — The Hinayana phase at Ajanta concluded around the 2nd century CE (with the decline of Satavahana power), and the Mahayana phase did not begin until approximately the 5th century CE under the Vakatakas — a gap of roughly 300 years.
• Reason (R): Correct — The Vakataka dynasty, especially under Harishena (r. c. 460–480 CE), was indeed the patron of the magnificent Mahayana-phase caves. Their patronage drove the artistic efflorescence that produced Ajanta's celebrated paintings.
• Causal link: Absent in the right direction — R explains who ended the gap (the Vakatakas), not why the gap occurred. The gap itself is explained by dynastic discontinuity, changing trade patterns, and the absence of a willing and capable patron for three centuries. R is a fact about the resolution of the gap, not its cause.

Value Addition:
• The intervening three centuries at Ajanta correspond roughly to the Vakataka predecessor period and several regional powers' reigns, none of which chose Ajanta as a patronage site.
• Harishena's reign is sometimes described as the golden age of Ajanta; he is specifically credited with Caves 1, 2, 16, 17, and others.
• The concept of a 'dark interval' in artistic production is found at other Indian sites too — e.g., Sanchi's construction also shows multi-phase patronage with intervening gaps.

(d) Cave 10

Cave 19 is a chaitya with notable sculptures but is smaller than Cave 26 and is not associated with the reclining Buddha.

Students who recall 'an elaborate later chaitya at Ajanta' may name Cave 19 without recalling the specific details (largest + reclining Buddha) that uniquely identify Cave 26. The reclining Buddha — one of the most famous individual sculptures at Ajanta — is the discriminating detail.
en.final_explanation:
Ajanta has five chaitya halls (Caves 9, 10, 19, 26, 29) spanning both phases. The largest and most elaborately decorated belongs to the Mahayana phase.

• Option (a) — Cave 26: Correct. Cave 26 is the largest chaitya hall at Ajanta and houses the famous reclining (parinirvana) Buddha carved into the side wall, along with elaborate makara toranas and flying apsaras.
• Option (b) — Cave 19: Incorrect. Cave 19 is an important Mahayana-phase chaitya with a prominent standing Buddha above the entrance and rich sculptural decoration, but it is smaller than Cave 26 and does not contain the reclining Buddha.
• Option (c) — Cave 9: Incorrect. Cave 9 is an early Hinayana-phase chaitya characterised by its plain stupa and minimal decoration — far from 'largest and most elaborate.'
• Option (d) — Cave 10: Incorrect. Cave 10 is also an early Hinayana chaitya, featuring some of the earliest painted narratives at Ajanta but no elaborate Mahayana-phase sculpture.

Value Addition:
• Cave 26's reclining Buddha is accompanied by a procession of mourning figures and celestial beings, depicting the scene of the Buddha's parinirvana.
• Cave 19 is notable for its sculptured facade with a large standing Buddha in the chaitya arch — a Mahayana iconographic innovation not found in Hinayana-era chaityas.
• Caves 9 and 10 contain some of the earliest surviving Buddhist paintings in the world, despite their plain architecture.

shared.concept_anchor: Continuous narration technique in Ajanta Jataka murals

en.display_text:
An art historian studying a large mural in one of the later caves at Ajanta observes that the same royal figure appears at least four times within a single unbroken pictorial field — first embarking on a sea voyage, then arriving at a foreign shore, then engaged in a forest renunciation, and finally depicted as an ascetic. There are no dividing lines or borders separating these scenes; they flow into one another within one composition.

Which narrative technique does this mural exemplify?

(a) Register system — where scenes are sequenced in horizontal bands separated by painted borders
(b) Synoptic representation — where a single moment is chosen to symbolically encapsulate the entire narrative
(c) Continuous narration — where multiple sequential episodes of the same story are depicted within a single unified pictorial space, with the protagonist appearing repeatedly
(d) Cameo composition — where key narrative figures are isolated in oval frames distributed across the mural surface
en.strong_distractor: a — Option a (register system) is deceptive because registers (horizontal bands separating scenes) are used in many ancient narrative traditions (Egyptian, Mesopotamian, and some Indian sculptural friezes) and students may recall this as a generic ancient narrative technique.
elimination_logic: The scenario describes multiple episodes of the same story shown within a single composition, with the protagonist appearing more than once — this is the definition of continuous narration.
Eliminate option a (register system) — registers separate distinct scenes into bands; the scenario describes them within a single unified space without division into horizontal bands.

Eliminate option b (synoptic representation) — synoptic representation typically shows a single key moment that encapsulates the entire narrative, not multiple sequential appearances of the protagonist.
Eliminate option d (cameo composition) — no such formal narrative technique is documented for Ajanta murals; this is a fabricated term.
Option c (continuous narration) correctly identifies the technique: a single pictorial space contains multiple sequential episodes of the same story.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The conflation trap conflates the register system (a real technique used in other ancient traditions) with continuous narration (the Ajanta technique). Both involve showing multiple scenes, but the register system uses horizontal bands to separate them, while continuous narration places them within a single unified pictorial field. Students who broadly recall 'sequential scenes' as a feature of ancient narrative art may choose the register option without knowing the specific Ajanta technique.
en.final_explanation:
Ajanta's Jataka murals employ a specific narrative technique that was sophisticated for its time and represents a distinct Indian approach to visual storytelling.

Applicable principle: Continuous narration — a single mural space contains multiple sequential episodes of the same story, with the same protagonist appearing repeatedly at different points in the narrative within one composition, without pictorial dividers between episodes.

• Option (a) — Register system: Incorrect. The register system divides a wall surface into horizontal bands, each containing a separate scene. Ajanta's Jataka murals do not use this convention; scenes flow within a unified pictorial space.
• Option (b) — Synoptic representation: Incorrect. Synoptic representation collapses an entire narrative into a single symbolic moment. Ajanta shows multiple moments, not one symbolically complete image.
• Option (c) — Continuous narration: Correct. The same figure (say, King Mahajanaka or the six-tusked elephant) appears multiple times across a single mural, at different narrative stages — this is continuous narration.
• Option (d) — Cameo composition: Incorrect. This term has no established meaning in the study of Ajanta or Indian art history; it is a fabricated option.

Value Addition:
• Continuous narration is also used in the sculptural friezes at Sanchi and Amaravati, predating Ajanta's painted examples.
• The technique requires the viewer to 'read' the painting by moving their gaze across it in sequence, much as one reads text.
• Similar continuous narration appears in Roman column reliefs (Trajan's Column) and Egyptian tomb paintings, suggesting it is a cross-cultural solution to sequential storytelling.

hi.display_text:
अजंता के बाद के गुफाओं में से एक में एक कला इतिहासकार एक बड़े भित्ति चित्र का अध्ययन कर रहा है और देखता है कि एक ही शाही आकृति कम से कम चार बार एक ही अविभाजित चित्रात्मक क्षेत्र में प्रकट होती है — पहले समुद्री यात्रा पर निकलती है, फिर विदेशी तट पर पहुँचती है, फिर वन में संन्यास लेती है, और अंत में एक तपस्वी के रूप में चित्रित होती है। इन दृश्यों को अलग करने वाली कोई विभाजक रेखाएँ या सीमाएँ नहीं हैं; वे एक ही रचना में एक-दूसरे में प्रवाहित होते हैं।

यह भित्ति चित्र कौन-सी कथात्मक तकनीक का उदाहरण है?

(a) रजिस्टर प्रणाली — जहाँ दृश्य क्षैतिज पट्टियों में क्रमबद्ध होते हैं जो चित्रित सीमाओं से अलग होते हैं
(b) सिनॉप्टिक प्रस्तुति — जहाँ एक क्षण को चुना जाता है जो पूरी कथा को प्रतीकात्मक रूप से समेटता है
(c) सतत कथन — जहाँ एक ही कहानी के कई क्रमिक प्रकरण एक एकीकृत चित्रात्मक स्थान में दिखाए जाते हैं, जिसमें नायक बार-बार प्रकट होता है
(d) कैमियो रचना — जहाँ मुख्य कथात्मक आकृतियाँ भित्ति चित्र की सतह पर अंडाकार फ्रेम में अलग की जाती हैं
hi.strong_distractor: a — विकल्प a (रजिस्टर प्रणाली) भ्रमित करने वाला है क्योंकि रजिस्टर (दृश्यों को अलग करने वाली क्षैतिज पट्टियाँ) कई प्राचीन कथात्मक परंपराओं (मिस्र, मेसोपोटामिया, और कुछ भारतीय मूर्तिकला फ्रिज़) में उपयोग होते हैं और छात्र इसे एक सामान्य प्राचीन कथात्मक तकनीक के रूप में याद कर सकते हैं।
elimination_logic: परिदृश्य में एक ही कहानी के कई प्रकरण एक ही रचना में दिखाए गए हैं, जिसमें नायक एक से अधिक बार प्रकट होता है — यह सतत कथन (continuous narration) की परिभाषा है।
विकल्प a (रजिस्टर प्रणाली) को हटा दें — रजिस्टर अलग-अलग दृश्यों को पट्टियों में विभाजित करते हैं; परिदृश्य में ये एक एकीकृत स्थान में बिना क्षैतिज पट्टियों के वर्णित हैं।
विकल्प b (सिनॉप्टिक प्रस्तुति) को हटा दें — सिनॉप्टिक प्रस्तुति आमतौर पर एक मुख्य क्षण दिखाती है जो पूरी कथा को समेटती है, न कि नायक के कई क्रमिक प्रकट होने को।
विकल्प d (कैमियो रचना) को हटा दें — अजंता भित्ति चित्रों के लिए ऐसी कोई औपचारिक कथात्मक तकनीक प्रलेखित नहीं है; यह एक निर्मित शब्द है।
विकल्प c (सतत कथन) सही तकनीक पहचानता है: एक ही चित्रात्मक स्थान में एक ही कहानी के कई क्रमिक प्रकरण होते हैं।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: मिश्रण जाल (conflation trap) रजिस्टर प्रणाली (जो अन्य प्राचीन परंपराओं में प्रयुक्त एक वास्तविक तकनीक है) को सतत कथन (अजंता की तकनीक) के साथ मिला देता है। दोनों में कई दृश्य दिखाए जाते हैं, लेकिन रजिस्टर प्रणाली क्षैतिज पट्टियों द्वारा उन्हें अलग करती है, जबकि सतत कथन उन्हें एक एकीकृत चित्रात्मक क्षेत्र में रखता है। जो छात्र 'क्रमिक दृश्य' को प्राचीन कथात्मक कला की विशेषता के रूप में सामान्यतः याद करते हैं, वे बिना अजंता की विशिष्ट तकनीक जाने रजिस्टर विकल्प चुन सकते हैं।
hi.final_explanation:
अजंता के जातक भित्ति चित्र एक विशिष्ट कथात्मक तकनीक का उपयोग करते हैं जो अपने समय के लिए परिष्कृत थी और भारतीय दृश्य कथा कहने के एक अलग दृष्टिकोण का प्रतिनिधित्व करती है।

लागू सिद्धांत: सतत कथन — एक ही भित्ति चित्र स्थान में एक ही कहानी के कई क्रमिक प्रकरण होते हैं, जिसमें नायक अलग-अलग कथात्मक चरणों में बार-बार प्रकट होता है, बिना प्रकरणों के बीच चित्रात्मक विभाजकों के।

• विकल्प (a) — रजिस्टर प्रणाली: गलत। रजिस्टर प्रणाली दीवार की सतह को क्षैतिज पट्टियों में विभाजित करती है, प्रत्येक में एक अलग दृश्य होता है। अजंता के जातक भित्ति चित्र इस परंपरा का उपयोग नहीं करते; दृश्य एक एकीकृत चित्रात्मक स्थान में प्रवाहित होते हैं।
• विकल्प (b) — सिनॉप्टिक प्रस्तुति: गलत। सिनॉप्टिक प्रस्तुति पूरी कथा को एक प्रतीकात्मक क्षण में समेटती है। अजंता कई क्षण दिखाता है, एक प्रतीकात्मक पूर्ण छवि नहीं।
• विकल्प (c) — सतत कथन: सही। एक ही आकृति (जैसे राजा महाजनक या छह-दांत वाला हाथी) एक ही भित्ति चित्र में कई बार, अलग-अलग कथात्मक चरणों में प्रकट होती है — यही सतत कथन है।
• विकल्प (d) — कैमियो रचना: गलत। इस शब्द का अजंता या भारतीय कला इतिहास में कोई स्थापित अर्थ नहीं है; यह एक निर्मित विकल्प है।

Value Addition:
